title: Bent around a ball
note: Spherical trigonometry, driven by the qibla.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-mathematics: 'Islam set its scholars a daily geometry problem: from any village on a round earth, find the direction of Makkah.' 'Al-Battani, observing from Raqqa on the Euphrates, sharpened the sine and cosine into working tools and measured the length of the solar year to within a couple of minutes of the modern value.' 'A triangle drawn on a ball behaves differently from a triangle drawn on a page.' 'Al-Battani's zij, his book of astronomical tables, was translated into Latin, and Copernicus cites him by name.' 'Every GPS fix and long haul flight path is computed with triangles on a sphere, their mathematics.' Person meta line: 'al-Battani, about 858 to 929 · Raqqa and Baghdad.'
research.retell: Because Muslims everywhere need to face Mecca to pray, an astronomer named al-Battani had to work out math for triangles on a curved earth instead of a flat page, and that same math still helps map things like planets and satellite signals today.

lines.text: Prayer set a hard geometry problem
Five times a day, face Makkah
lines.sub: from any village on a round earth

lines.text: On a flat page a triangle makes 180
On a ball it always makes more
So the way to Makkah is an arc
lines.sub: not a straight line on a flat map

lines.text: The old flat rules quietly fail
So he built the mathematics of curves
lines.sub: your GPS still uses triangles on a ball
